predecessors.name: Himyarite Kingdom
predecessors.text: central Arabia (Najd and the Yamama), the Ma'add confederation's land, over which Himyar installed Hujr

ledger.x: c. 450: Hujr, a Kindite prince backed by Himyar, founds the Banu Akil al-Murar kingdom over the Ma'add of central Arabia. Kinda page: 'In the mid-5th century, part of the Kinda, with support from Himyar, migrated' into central and northern Arabia; the Himyarite king gave Ma'add's kingship to Hujr. The year is the…

c. 528: al-Harith ibn Amr, the greatest Kindite king, is slain and the kingdom breaks up. Kinda page: 'There, in 528, he was slain by the Lakhmid king al-Mundhir III'; the kingdom 'lasted until the mid-6th century', by when its rulers had been killed or had fled to Hadramawt. Kingdom of Kindah infobox ends c. 528. The…

wars.name: Kindite capture of al-Hira
wars.outcome: Al-Harith captured al-Hira, ruled it briefly, then turned to the Byzantines.

wars.name: Kindite-Lakhmid war (death of al-Harith)
wars.outcome: Al-Harith was slain by the Lakhmid king al-Mundhir III (or by the Banu Kalb); the Kindite kingdom fell apart.

certainty.note: A tribal hegemony in the desert interior: no frontier is described by any page.
